candidates.name: Víctor Raúl Haya de la Torre

elections.notes: No candidate reached the one-third of the vote the constitution required, and the results were annulled after a military coup on 18 July 1962, so no president was proclaimed. Víctor Raúl Haya de la Torre, who received the most votes, is marked as the winner here, but he never took office. Others combines the Socialist Party (16,658) and the Progressive Social Movement (9,202). The election was re-run in 1963.

Alejandro Toledo boycotted the run-off, in which over 30% of ballots were declared invalid; Fujimori later resigned and new elections were held in 2001. Turnout is for the run-off; the first round's was 82.83%.

elections.notes: Shares are of valid votes; blank votes (2,190,059 in the first round, 121,489 in the run-off) and invalid votes are excluded. Pedro Castillo won the run-off by 44,263 votes and was proclaimed president-elect on 19 July 2021. Turnout is for the run-off; the first round's was 70.05%. Region winners are each department's run-off winner, from the article's second-round results-by-department table (24 of 26 map regions). The table has a single Lima row covering both Lima Metropolitan and Lima region, so those two get no winner; the Peruvians abroad row is left out.
